question: Why did the p95 latency go up on 05 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The increase in p95 latency is due to a reduction in the search db.pool_size, leading to connection pool exhaustion.
why_chain: The db.pool_size was reduced from 50 to 5, causing the connection pool to be exhausted more frequently.
This exhaustion leads to waiting for a free connection, which is recorded in logs.
The waiting for a free connection results in a WARN message, which is recorded in logs.
The WARN message is escalated to an alert, indicating the p95 latency exceeded the service level objective (SLO).

contributing_factors.description: The increase in p95 latency is also due to the increase in request volume, which put more strain on the system.
why_chain: The request volume increased by 9% after the change, putting more pressure on the system.
The increased request volume led to more frequent connection pool exhaustion.
The connection pool exhaustion resulted in more WARN messages in logs.
The WARN messages were escalated to alerts, indicating the p95 latency exceeded the SLO.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in p95 latency is due to a change in the service architecture.
ruled_out.reason: No evidence supports a change in the service architecture, only a change in configuration.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in p95 latency is due to a change in the external database.
ruled_out.reason: No evidence supports a change in the external database, only a change in the internal database pool size.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in p95 latency is due to a change in the network configuration.
ruled_out.reason: No evidence supports a change in the network configuration, only a change in the internal database pool size.

evidence.summary: P95 latency for service search rose from 140 ms to 290 ms (+107%), with a change point at 2026-03-05T03:15:00Z.
The change is concentrated in service search: 3 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.02).
At the same time, request volume for service search stayed about the same (2514 per 5 min before, 2741 per 5 min after, +9%).
At the same time, error rate for service search rose (0.40% before, 0.62% after, +53%).
Changed search db.pool_size from 50 to 5 (all regions) (search; 2 min before the change; record R011)
search: WARN connection pool exhausted, waiting for a free connection (search, eu-west; 3 min after the change; record R012)
p95 latency above SLO on search (search; 15 min after the change; record R013)
search: WARN connection pool exhausted, waiting for a free connection (search, ap-south; 20 min after the change; record R014)
search: WARN connection pool exhausted, waiting for a free connection (search, us-east; 26 min after the change; record R015)

reasons: ✓ A change event (config_changes) lines up in time (2 min before the change).
✓ 4 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✓ Request volume stayed steady, ruling out a traffic spike.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.

actions.action: Increase the db.pool_size back to 50 to prevent connection pool exhaustion.
Monitor request volume and adjust capacity if it exceeds the current limits.
Implement a retry mechanism for connection pool exhaustion to reduce the impact on latency.
